findings.title: Feature check runs before CLI validation, masking usage errors with exit code 4
findings.body: In `run()`, the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES)` check executes before `validateConfig()`. As a result, an invocation with invalid usage (e.g. missing the required `--file` argument) made while the feature is disabled exits with code 4 (`FEATURE_DISABLED`) and never reports the actual usage problem, even though the documentation in `update-compatibility.adoc` states exit code 2 signals an invalid CLI option and exit code 1 an unexpected error. Scripts keying on exit codes cannot distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'you invoked the command wrongly'. The same ordering exists in `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()`. Consider running the feature check after CLI validation, or documenting that the feature check takes precedence.

findings.title: Default (null) update strategy path deploys without rolling-updates feature, leaving new operator requirement untested
findings.body: The docs added in this PR state that while `rolling-updates` is in preview, the Keycloak Operator will fail if the feature is not enabled. However, `createInitialDeployment(null)` returns early without enabling the feature, so the default-strategy test case runs with the feature disabled. If the operator's default path indeed requires the feature (as the docs caution implies), this test would fail against such an operator; if the default path deliberately does not require it, there is no test asserting the operator's failure behavior when `spec.update.strategy` is set without enabling `rolling-updates`. A test covering the 'strategy set but feature disabled' failure case is missing.
